newsitem.title: USA: Fran's center expected at coast late Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Fran's center expected at coast late Thursday.

text.p: At 5:00 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), the center of Hurricane Fran was near latitude 32.9 north and longitude 77.9 west or about 80 miles (129 km) south-southeast of South Carolina's border with North Carolina, the National Hurricane Center said.
That position also put the storm about 95 miles (153 km) south of Wilmington, N.C.

Fran was moving toward the north-northwest near 16 mph (26 kmh) and a gradual turn toward the north was expected Thursday night or on Friday. On that track, its center was expected to cross the coast shortly before midnight, although hurricane force winds were beginning to sweep across the coast in a wide stretch of the hurricane warned area.

Maximum sustained winds were near 115 mph (185 kmh). Hurricane force winds extended outward up to 140 miles (225 km) from the center and tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 260 miles (418 km).

Hurricane warnings were in effect from Edisto Beach, South Carolina to North Carolina's border with Virginia and a hurricane watch and a tropical storm warning were in effect from north of the North Carolina/Virginia border to Chincoteague, Virginia. A tropical storm warning also was in effect for the lower Chesapeake Bay and from north of Brunswick, Georgia, to just south of Edisto Beach.

Forecasters also were tracking tropical depression eight. At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), the depression's center was located near latitude 114.6 north and longitude 53.1 west, or about 535 miles (860 km) east of the Leeward Islands of the Caribbean Sea. The depression was moving west near 13 mph (20 kmh), with maximum sustained winds of 35 mph (55 kmh). Some strengthening was expected.
When winds reached 39 mph (63 kmh), the depression would become Tropical Storm Hortense.
